mechanismReference.note: Reference-only source audit for the float-triangle projection; formal execution does not claim or require a jpegli binary.

claimBoundary: The raw-plane probe uses libjpeg's public raw_data_out path with accurate integer IDCT and writes tight post-IDCT Y/Cb/Cr planes before chroma upsampling and YCbCr-to-RGB conversion. This intentionally holds entropy decode and IDCT constant for all reconstruction candidates.

The independent oracle implements the pinned libjpeg-turbo 3.2.0 integer h2v2 fancy interpolation and YCbCr-to-RGB tables outside libjpeg. fancy-h-fancy-v must reproduce one-shot djpeg RGB byte-for-byte; failure is fatal and no tolerance is introduced.

The float-triangle-quantized-idct candidate is a deliberately narrower projection inspired by jpegli's floating-point 3/4-1/4 upsampling and floating-point BT.601 conversion: it starts from the same already-quantized libjpeg raw post-IDCT planes and removes only subsequent intermediate integer rounding. It is not a jpegli decode, does not model jpegli float dequantization/IDCT or dequantization bias, and can only falsify the hypothesis that post-IDCT reconstruction rounding alone explains the cross-backend residual.

The mixed-axis candidates replace exactly one reconstruction axis with nearest replication while preserving the same raw planes and integer YCbCr conversion. Their distance to ImageCraft/ImageIO is an attribution observation, not a production tolerance or proof of perceptual superiority.
This experiment is source-bound mechanism evidence. It does not claim that ImageIO exposes or internally uses any named filter merely because one candidate is numerically closer.
